Details: Dec 21, 2024 ·  Lead / Redpoint. I didn’t actually do the start, but I will go back (have fresh beta now) and finish this climb. Went up and around a boulder on the left to avoid the spicy start.  Started up about 8’ off the ground then fade climbed over to the crack.  You can put a .2 in down low for the actual start but I don’t know if it would save you from a ground fall.    Very bouldery start.  The rest was okay, agree with 1 star.   My ego would have me go back to prove not being scared but that’s not the point of climbing for me.  It’s about learning and not falling into unhelpful thought patterns(lifelong process), but having fun connecting with nature and community.  My ego is not always my amigo.

Details:
Jan 28, 2026 ·  Lead. Lead P2

Gear: Doubles of 0.3 to 3, and one 4. Need 70m for the rappel
Descent: Rappel off the bolts, same as Left Ski Track

P1: Start in the middle of the three cracks. Once this crack ends, turn right and make a move left. You’ll see a slightly more vertical section with a long flake-like crack system that takes good gear. Continue up this until you see a cave. Stem and get your left foot on a good hold, and reach around for a good right hand. Continue up a slab section, go far left for super easy moves up a featured slab. Scramble up to a small notch (which is the beginning of the second pitch). Made a gear anchor with a 0.75, 0.3, and Metolius 0.2

P2: Traverse is pretty straightforward but there is a slick and polished right foot that my foot slipped off of and did not inspire confidence. Used a 0.5 right in the beginning, 1 and 2 after that

Details:
Mar 29, 2025 ·  Follow. This route is definitely an old school Joshua tree “5.7”. Most of it is 5.8/5.9 but overhang traverse has some greasy 5.10+ moves with no feet, all upper body. 
If you or your partner is newer to multi-pitch, save yourself a stressful situation and avoid this route. 
At P2, the lead will not be able to see or hear their follower once they are at the anchor. If the follower can’t get through or slips during in the overhang traverse section, they will be flailing mid air and need slack to start over, but the lead won’t be able to see or hear them. I can confidently lead 5.8/5.9 and had to bail on this one. With the zig zag of the rope across the traverse, removing gear is very difficult and I would have needed a traxion to cheat through it. 
Walkie talkies would’ve been helpful too.

Oct 4, 2025 ·  Lead / Fell/Hung. Great climb but I was unable to do the crux. I don’t have the length for going from the bolt to the crack in hand jam but it is possible to do it with layback. It is just really hard to do it. 
Placements. 
Before the bolt I place a 1 at the entrance above the big rock I use as hand. Then a .3 while going up riding the horse in a small crack. 
Clipped the bolt riding the horse but was still hard because I barely reached. 
I tried to do the move to get into the crack with a toe hook but I was unable to get into it. 
Then I threw a .75 and clipped it just to get into the crack system and work the crack. The placement was really bad and I had to change it placing same pro above. The crack is painful and slippery so it is really hard to move in that section. I had to pull into the gear to finish the climb. Crack is great after that but pro is hard to place because of the crack shape. I used bunch of .75, 2x .3, 2x 2, 3, and maybe something small going up the crack

The route was super cool, following a dihedral until a roof with an insane pocket. After I reached up over the roof, I was faced with grooves in the wall that provided plenty of options for hands and feet, but which were difficult crimps and pinches after getting to that point. All in all we both walked away happy having topped a harder (but more appropriately graded) climb.

Details:
Nov 16, 2024 ·  Lead / Onsight. Started on the right side of the rock getting into a hand/finger crack. Place a small piece maybe .4. Went over to the traverse. Place #3 and other 2 smaller pieces maybe .3 and .4. The traverse has great hands to jam but the feet is poor. Had to be creative but always had the foot on something. To get into the vertical crack had to smirror right foot in the type of arete for feet, left foot high in a chip and jammed hand in the crack. Placed a .5 at the start and then when going up placed .75 and .3 and some other medium piece. Then there is a bolt in the slab section. After clipping got a side pool on the left once feet are above the bolt. Put left put on a small feature and started to move to the left until I was in a positive position. Pushed hard on that slab and got to the top. Placed the anchor in the horizontal crack closer to the bolted belay station and extended the anchor. 
I did enjoyed very much that climb.

Details:
Mar 15, 2026 ·  Lead / Pinkpoint. Second attempt got it clean on the gear I placed on the first attempt.

Start is a bit dicey. First crux due to thin flaring crack at start. Can place good gear to prevent decking.

Go up and place two pieces to protect to start 
Metolius offset blue/yellow
Maybe metiolius offset yellow/orange for second.

Use sling extension for a yellow #2 BD C4

Roof crux:
Great undercling sidepull on left wall.
Protect roof finger crack with a yellow totem and then black totem.
Used lie backing moves to get into it.
Good foot out left when you are high in the crack.

Crack disappears and becomes a sloppier. Keep going and you’ll find an ok flared hand jam. It’s enough to get your weight into to pull up your feet.

Can protect the follower with either an orange totem (better than a BD because crack is flared)

Or just put rope around rock which will protect fine.
Then go left to the mussy hook anchors.

Gear Placed (didn’t record order)

1. Metolius Offset Blue/yellow
2. BD C3 Yellow 2
3. BD C3 Red 1
4. BD C4 #1
5. Metolius Offset Yellow/ Red
6. Totem Orange
7. BD C4 #2 extend with sling
8. BD Z4 0.75 
9. BD C4 0.4
10. Totem Green
11. Metolius Offset Red/Black
12. Metolius Offset Purple/Blue
13. Metolius Offset Yellow/ Orange

Roof:
14. BD C4 #3 (5 ft below)
15. Totem Yellow
16. Totem Black

Optional save Totem Orange for protecting follower falling at roof. Or route rope around the flake.

right foot in the pod, bump right ring lock up, get it good. 0.3z4. left foot smear, stay square and stand into a high left lock above the horizontal, high right foot to the decent toe jam, also get it good, then stay square and stand up high into the hight right hand jug. palm press and get the foot on the smear and stand

start beta:
get the crimps, right foot up, left foot way out. grab seam with right, engage thumb, left foot up drop knee, right foot up to the crimp. then match seam and pistol squat

Starts right, moving left delicately on slab, matching both crimps to a left side pull, bump it slightly to get a good lie back crimp and higher better left foot, with right foot on left horizontal crimp. Stand up and place red #1 in pod, left hand on sidepull pocket with right hand on lower pod to keep balance. Lay back to right hand on jug bump right foot to red pod and place a green .75 to protect crux. Just above the green grab pod with left hand left foot out on small foot right foot into small pod crank and grab crimp. Once at crimp, high left foot and slowly stand, grabbing left sidepull/crack with left hand. Stand and put right foot on crimp. Double gaston to get left foot out on jib. Place a #2 in pod above head and work way up. Don’t forget a .5 to protect traverse after crack

Details:
Oct 26, 2025 ·  Lead / Onsight. Wow. This is a great route. I overlooked it for years, but the second pitch is one of the best moderate chimneys I’ve climbed in my life. Final slab has incredible position, and the first pitch has almost too many holds. We did the 5.6 traverse start, which was pretty damn scrunchy for a 6’4” 180lb man, maybe the crux of the whole climb. I don’t think I placed anything smaller than a #1 camalot. A #4 was particularly useful on the second pitch, and won’t get wasted on the first. If new to JTree or the grade/style, bumping a #5 up the second pitch would probably keep you on a TR through the crux, though this is only speculative. A nice outing for climbers of any grade.

Glad all the lead bolts besides the last got chopped. So many bolt shafts next to a perfectly good crack.

Details: Dec 28, 2022 ·  Lead / Fell/Hung. Red BD offset at the crux was bomber but too shallow for me to feel great about relying on it to prevent a deck fall. The orange mastercam tucked under the block below was great, though -points for the skrittley rock quality. It was almost good enough for me to trust it as the only thing between me and the deck. If I slowed down and placed a larger cam on either side of the chockstone/ block below that would have eased my fears… but I didn’t and instead pulled into the upper crack with only the skrittley orange master cam to prevent the long fall (+ two cams in the lower crack that were too far down to do anything) and then proceeded to pump out in a baggy but juggy right finger lock as I contemplated the stickiness of my small offset stopper… if I had known the next hold was über positive I would have salvaged the onsight- but alas- that word “if” has made it into another tick report. All in all I give it a 5.9+, no PG-13 though, the small risk of decking at the crux can easily be mitigated with more forethought and less confidence. And the 9+ may just be a 9* (5.9 with a touch of COVID)

Name: Carrie Van Lanen
Details: Feb 9, 2024 ·  Follow. Followed Louis. Hangdogged this. Go up the chimney in the back side (protect with a 2 before the traverse and a 3 along the way. Build anchor from .75, gold offset nut, .3 or .4. Place good .4 (or two)and ok blue offset but before the dyno. LH underclinging nub, RH in crack, LF high, RF up to sloper, dropknee and go statically if tall/strong enough. Place .75. Work right and up into crack. Work both cracks for a bit until transitioning into a strenuous lieback in the right crack (.5 placements). Plac a coupe mediocre .4’a before the OW. Can get a 5 in the OW, but be careful of walking it. Strain through the tight OW for a bit until it chimneys out. Belay from rap anchor setback  ~20 ft from edge. Rap off.

Name: Ben T
Details: Jan 12, 2025 ·  Lead. Aided it. The safest way down is to break down the anchor and have your partner lower you over the back right side (put the rope over a small feature near the front side summit so it doesn't get caught in the crack) to the ledge. This works fine if you end with TR, but only works for lead-follow if you lower your partner back to the base so they can in turn lower you over the opposite side. Then find an easy downclimb ~100' feet to climber's right, which ends with a very low angle offwidth. Or rap off a large boulder behind the ledge that you lowered to.

Name: Cosmic Hotdog
Details:
Nov 2, 2024 ·  Lead / Fell/Hung. Every bit as burly as I remember! Felt good to lead the whole thing myself this time. 

Microcams and small nuts (DMM gold and smaller) protect up to and including the roof. An offset .3/.4 protects the opening move off the deck + a 0.1 protects the move above that before leaping for the small rock horn. Black totems through finger size pieces protect above the roof to the finish. 
Beta is to layback the rail, get the feet established on tiny edges and jump for the small horn (right hand). 

A few hand size for the very top as well as for the anchor (anchor takes #4, #3, #2).

Details:
Jan 31, 2026 ·  Lead / Onsight. Led first pitch with Brandon! Very fun route! First pitch kind of gradually progressed in difficulty with two distinct cruxes closer to the top.

Everything is there (including gear). Black totems and BD 0.3s were life savers here.

The feet on the top crux aren’t particularly good, but stemming between feet on the left and right side, get you high enough to get the good holds.

Brandon led the second pitch and it was my very first 10a TRonsight! The moves are delicate and balance-y, and there’s just enough gear placements to keep it safe.

We finished out left and the climbing after the crux is easy and straight forward.

Excellent climb!

Details:
Nov 2, 2025 · 1 pitch.  Lead / Onsight. Amazing climb. I brought almost double on everything but only used couple of doubles. Bolted anchor. Crux at the top of pitch one. I only did pitch one. 
List of placement bottom up: 

First vertical crack: 
1. (2) in the big square hole. 
2 and 3 (.5)
4. Yellow Metolius 

Horizontal crack I didn’t place anything. 

Second vertical crack (second from left to right. Don’t get confused going to the first one you see in front of you): 

5. (.75)
6. (2)
7. (1)
8. (.3) 

Second horizontal crack to the left: 
9. (.75) 

Second and last vertical crack: 
10. Gray Metolius 00
11. (0)
Those last 2 placements were at the small finger crack and for the hand I layback with right hand, right foot on a notch to continue up. Get the better holds up right and transfer feet to the left. Stand up and above are the anchors.

Details:
Mar 15, 2026 ·  Lead / Redpoint. Actually felt a bit hard this time.
Maybe because it was in the sun and getting slippery.
Or more likely because i tried going right too quickly below the first bolt.
Go up high to the good jug on the left. Then transitioning right is no problem.

Bring a 5th QuickDraw for the piton. Seems ok and might as well add in.

Can protect in crack leading to first bolt if no stick clip.

Panic draws are helpful for the second and third bolt. And forth is not bring a 5th QuickDraw.

Crack gloves help at first bolt crux

Don’t need a #2 for the top section. It’s super secure when you are there. Hand jams to the top.

Around piton height there are good side crimps around left of Arete.

Details:
Dec 7, 2025 ·  Lead / Redpoint. Got the red point on Western Saga!

Beginning was easy, but I couldn’t find any pro that kept me off the ground until I was probably like 20ft off the deck. The climbing was relatively easy, but I really wanted something.

Felt like I cruised most of the rest of the climb. Placed two pieces where I could and ran it out to the ledge.

Dihedral had a perfect hand jam to start, it’s just kind of a yard on a hand jam and smear to get established. The rest of the dihedral was fun! Sort of layback-y on hand jams with at least two good rests. Definitely wasn’t the crux for me.

Pulled the roof with a purple totem and a #4 right below it. The foot is super duper good, but you do need to pull on a hand jam using a pretty secure chock stone to do the actual pull. It was totally secure, but I definitely questioned if I wanted to trust it.

There was also a part that I needed to stand up on a pretty high foot, but the hands were good so it was easy to get up. 

Good enough jams the rest of the way up!

Second 5.9 lead in Jtree!

Maybe leave the hat in the ground next time. It got kind of annoying with the move right under the roof.

Name: Carrie Van Lanen
Details:
Feb 15, 2024 · 2 pitches.  Lead. Joe’s first day in JTree. Did it as 2 pitches.
Start from large flat boulder just right if a large detached flake resting along the slab. Place a .5 to keep the rope high and protect a swing off the first couple moves (feet slippery), then complete 4th class slab runout to anchor at a horizontal (.5 - 1). P2 lead up to crack and place .4 or .5 in the small slot just left. Then placed 1, 2, 3 on the lead. Belay from a horizontal just below the top from mix of 2’s & 3’s. Then 3rd-4th class, low consequence walk up through “chimney” to top. Several descent options:
South downclimb goes down a slab (real consequence of you botch the last friction step down) followed by medium difficulty chimney downclimb -OR- summit to climbers left and then follow the northern downclimb (heads up 15 foot slab section getting down from summit) OR don’t walk up after P2 and instead climb right to bolted rap station (fastest and lowest consequence if roped up.)

Details: Mar 16, 2025 ·  Lead / Onsight. Gear felt pretty solid, brought doubles to 2 plus some nuts. Used a .4 totem, then a green bd nut and a black totem to protect the first crux, fingers in the pod with the black totem. Stem up and use that little foot chip to reposition. Name: Yosemite Joe
Details:
Nov 17, 2025 ·  TR. Got the beta worked out (watch vid)
As far as placing the crux piece, might need another sesh. 
PS. From the wide stem, you’ll higher right hand jam, then grab top of the horn with left. 
Place gear from this stance with right hand. 
Once done, maybe shake out, then bump right foot to tall edge, then left foot. 
Right and to pod, right foot to dish, left hand to sidepull, right hand to sidepull. Bring up left foot done. 

My guess is hold the horn with the left hand, stemming, preslung 2 or 4 on right side of harness. Bring feet up and gun it with right hand to intermediate pod, bring right foot up in scoop above piece, left hand to sidepull, right hand just above that, bring left foot up to a stance, then with left hand grab a quickdraw on left side of harness and clip. OR left finger jam in constriction slightly higher and then beyond bomber hand jam above that and still clip with left. 
Gear probably triples .75-2 doubles .5 and 3 + 4 + extra 2

Name: Alonso Rodriguez
Details:
Feb 16, 2025 ·  Lead / Fell/Hung. Still hard…. 
Beta: There’s a big chalk hold about 15-20 feet up that fits a #4 perfectly! 2 pods below that fits a 0.75 totem (must be a totem!) Reaching this pod requires a bit of a runout from an initial 0.4 totem near the ground. 

There are 3 good hand pods. First one is about 8 ft off the ground while the other two are right next to each other and 12 ft off the ground. Do NOT place cams in these pods as they are crucial hand holds. 

Sequence, RH in lowest pod. LH in middle pod. RH cross to final pod right above middle pod. From there, place the green totem and either down climb to rest or fire up to the bomber hand jam. From there, you can place a 4. Hard LB sequence + big move to a LH sloper and really high right foot right above the #4

Name: Andrew W
Details:
Feb 13, 2024 ·  Follow. Followed my gear bc Amy didn’t want to climb this, thanks for being a good sport and super patient. The rap was super annoying but a short move into a squeeze chimney traverse to the climbers right gets to north overhang bolts pretty easily and it reaches with the 80m we were using. Also I felt more confident but didn’t not get my TR go clean.

Gear beta:

Until bolt:
#2, Green totem (not recommended), #4, bolt

After bolt before super slab:
Offset 0.75/0.5, Green tricam, (1) #3, (2) #2, (2) #1, (2) #0.75
-> could take more of any of these sizes. 

Super slab before top:
(2) #3, (1) #5

Anchor:
Takes 0.3, 0.4, 0.5, 0.75 on right, but is most secure with a 1, 2, 3 and/or 4 on the left. 

Tips for next time:
-Ground fall isn’t worth it at the bottom, instead it can be worth it to just get the #4 and/or bolt via aid.
-Get better rests higher by a higher/bigger left foot.
-At the crux sequence, just go fast and confident.
-Push on after the bolt to get to the rests.
-Follow the prior beta to pull the crux.

each move crosses over the next
Rh hand jam, Lh finger stack, Rh bad hand jam w the thumb tucked into the pam, Lh fudged finger jam however it fits, Rh pinch the higher 2 of the 3 small pods, Lh sinker hand jam, Rh pulling on the positive end of that rail which makes the hand jam. obv be working feet up the whole time but now it becomes very important. there is a high left foot chip and a dish-esquw feature in the right. begin laying back so the right foot can go onto the dish, left foot moves up so the right foot can go into the glorious hand jam section. the hard part is over, now fight the pump

Details: Jan 17, 2025 ·  Lead / Onsight. 5.7 variation: up the dark chimney through an exposed section to a weird offwidth off left you can stem into, then a few slab moves to a belay in the big horizontal. Name: Carrie Van Lanen
Details: Jan 17, 2025 ·  Lead / Onsight. Led P1&2. With Glenn & Mark. P1 don’t go too deep. .75 protects before pulling onto the face.  But runout for a bit after that. Placed up to a size 2 near the top. Moved left and belayed from .5 -2 in horizontal crack. Felt comfy unroping on the ledge to the left, but wouldn’t do that if guiding. P2 heads up the flaring chimney. Protected P2 with an orange totem and then a # 4 higher when I veered left towards the fist crack. Belayed from behind a large flake just left of the fist crack with sizes 2,3, and 4. Glenn lead P3 fist crack super short. Get into the crack and place #3 and/or .5. Crux is shortly off the deck. Pro higher is #4 and #2. Belayed from large tricam, 1, and 3. Rapped Mikes books.

Details:
Jan 2, 2026 ·  TR. 3x burns with Colette. 

BETA: From the bottom start with good right hand and left hand full span. And right foot up to tick. Then left foot to good slopey rail. Stand and bring left hand across int highest finger crack inverted. Bump right hand I think inverted. Then bump left foot to higher rail. And right foot to higher chip.  Cross right hand over into crack. And bump feet higher and stand. Potentially place gear here or go up left hand inverted to crack and then right hand to crimp and place here. The gear is a .2 yellow z4. Bump left foot and right foot to obvious ticks and toss left hand high to sidepull it. Move body right too at the same time to make it a better hold. Move left foot to a little chip. Press on the crimps with right palm and bring up right foot for opposition. Then just stand up into this and place a black totem. Theres a left hand jam here to rest!! Then move up into a left hand finger lock. Then do some moves to get an inverted right hand into the next good pocket with a left foot jammed in the lower crack. Use a red z4 here above. Ideally something bigger than aThen you have to start moving into layback to the right. And you have a foot ja for either the left or right foot. Probably right foot. And focus on getting the left hand into the upper layback with a semi thumb catch. Plug in a black totem in the triple lined hole with the right foot in the foot jam. Stand up through it into a pinky and the finger next to it in a non inverted finger stack. Keep standing through it with maybe the left foot tucked to the rock heel against the rock. Then cross right hand up and over. Drop 2nd and 3rd finger int the top of it. Not the pinky! Pinky goes under the flare. Move feet and bring left hand up and over into flaring hand/finger press. Keep going up in the crack with right hand or go over to the right with the sloper. You’re done!

Make anchor with 2 number 4s an extend over lip

Gear in order. Yellow .2 z4, black totem, red .2 z4. Black totem.
